answer: An agent market requires each identity to lock $100 in escrow for 90 days before it can vote on job disputes, with one vote per funded identity. Whether an agent maps a reef, surveys karst, or labels a graph vertex, the same rule applies. An attacker seeking 1,000 votes must immobilize $100,000 for three months, paying financing costs and losing access to that capital; generating more keys alone buys no influence.
